text: Most of Tatum’s injury rehabilitation has taken place away from the public eye, but his workout Monday morning offered a peek behind the curtains. At Seaholm High School, where the Celtics held shootaround before their game against the Detroit Pistons, several assistant coaches, including Tony Dobbins, put Tatum through a series of on-court drills. He flashed his typical outside touch and showcased the physical progress he has made over the eight months since rupturing his Achilles last spring.Tatum did shooting drills simulating coming off screens. He worked on his pull-up jump shots. He drove through contact from Dobbins, who was playing the role of defender. Tatum rose for a few dunks during the workout as well. He was not available for comment afterward, but teammate Derrick White said it has been “amazing to see” Tatum’s progress.New York Times

text: Ian Begley: Josh Hart is returning to the court today with an ankle that is less than 100 percent healthy.Why not wait for the ankle to fully heal? Hart says his impatience, competitiveness and the Knicks' recent skid factored in to his decision to play today vs. DAL: "I want to be out there to try to help the team as much as I can so (the team's recent struggles) did (influence his decision) a little bit; a combination of that, there’s the competitiveness and the impatience that I display," Hart said before the Mavs game.He missed Saturday's loss to Phoenix with lingering ankle soreness. It's the same ankle that caused him to miss eight games from Dec. 25-Jan. 9. The Knicks have gone 3-6 in their games without Hart. Overall, they've dropped eight of their past 10 games. Hart was asked to diagnose what has gone wrong for the Knicks lately. "If I could, I don’t think we’d be in this stretch. I don’t know; I think it’s a combination of stuff," Hart said. "Just gotta be better defensively, more physical, into the ball, more effort, more energy. That kind of stuff. I can’t say that I’m surprised because obviously January – middle of January, especially- those are the kind of dog days of the season. So not too surprised (with Knicks' recent record); you kind of see a few teams around (the NBA) kind of showing that fatigure. You know it happens every year. And then kind of refresh at All Star, right after All Star and kind of just carry that through. So, you know, it happens."x.com
